data.title: Insulin activation of Rheb, a mediator of mTOR/S6K/4E-BP signaling, is inhibited by TSC1 and 2
data.authors: Garami A; Zwartkruis FJ; Nobukuni T; Joaquin M; Roccio M; Stocker H; Kozma SC; Hafen E; Bos JL; Thomas G

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Insulin activates Rheb-GTP, inhibited by TSC1/2, positioning Rheb as the direct upstream activator of TOR.
data.abstract_excerpt: Tumor suppressor genes evolved as negative effectors of mitogen and nutrient signaling pathways, such that mutations in these genes can lead to pathological states of growth. Tuberous sclerosis (TSC) is a potentially devastating disease associated with mutations in two tumor suppressor genes, TSC1 and 2, that function as a complex to suppress signaling in the mTOR/S6K/4E-BP pathway. However, the inhibitory target of TSC1/2 and the mechanism by which it acts are unknown.

extracted_findings.effect: Insulin activates Rheb, a mediator of mTOR/S6K/4E-BP signaling, and this is inhibited by TSC1/2
